Token counts exclude the beginning-of-sequence position (Table~\ref{tab:bos}).}
  \label{tab:setup}
  \begin{tabular}{ll}
    \toprule
     &  \\
    \midrule

    Layers graded & 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24 \\
    SAE & \texttt{gemma-2-2b-res-matryoshka-dc}, Matryoshka, $D = 32,768$ \\
    Nested blocks & B0 $[0,128)$, B1 $[128,512)$, B2 $[512,2048)$, B3 $[2048,8192)$, B4 $[8192,32768)$ \\

    Firing threshold & $a_f > 0.001$ post-JumpReLU \\
    Edge criterion & $R \geq 0.5$, fire $\geq 20$, co-fire $\geq 30$ \\
    Reconstruction gate & both relative gains $\geq 0.01$ \\
    $S_\mathrm{res}$ rule & both decoders in the top $k = 5$ \\
    Sibling flag & mean pairwise Jaccard $\geq 0.5$ \\

    Superparent gate & fan-out $\geq 30\%$ of the child block \\

% [INT 2]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The metric set.} Eight questions about the same edge, plus an unnumbered in-block measurement that grades same-level pairs rather than candidate edges. Metric~1 defines the candidate set and 2--8 grade it: 2--5 weigh a single edge with increasingly demanding evidence, from chance to frequency to reconstruction to meaning, and 6--8 widen the view from one edge to the parent's whole neighbourhood. Metric~4 is named honestly as a \emph{contribution filter} rather than as Tree SAE's $S_\mathrm{res}$: two strong but unrelated co-firing features pass both of its legs, and its pass rate scales with block energy. The probe-based $S_\mathrm{res}$ is metric~5, and its target is the self-label $\mathbf{1}[f_c > 0]$, so a corrupted latent yields a probe that validates its own corruption; we report it as self-labeled and as a self-consistency check, not as ground truth.}
  \label{tab:battery}
  \begin{tabular}{llllr}
    \toprule
     & Metric & What it asks & Threshold & Module \\
    \midrule
    1a & Reverse coverage $R$ & $P(\text{parent} \mid \text{child})$ & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{coverage} \\
    1b & Forward coverage $F$ & $P(\text{child} \mid \text{parent})$ & reported & \texttt{coverage} \\
    2 & Independence null & PMI against independent firing & $> 0$ & \texttt{independence\_null} \\
    3 & Token-frequency control & does the edge survive on rare tokens & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{token\_control} \\
    4 & Reconstruction ablation & both features carry mass on the child's tokens & $\geq 0.01$ & \texttt{reconstruction} \\
    5 & Probe $S_\mathrm{res}$ & both decoders near the child-concept probe & top-5 rank & \texttt{sres} \\
    6 & Out-degree & one parent covering most of the next block & $\geq 30\%$ & \texttt{outdegree} \\
    7 & Sibling redundancy & co-activation among one parent's children & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{sibling\_redundancy} \\
    8 & Joint-child coverage & $R_\mathrm{supp}$, $R_\mathrm{mass}$, energy share & reported & \texttt{joint\_child} \\
    --- & In-block directed coverage & containment within one block, and duplicates & asymmetry & \texttt{in\_block\_edges} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

% [INT 3]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{Three tiers, trading ground truth against realism.} Each rung licenses the one above it: Tier~1 proves the arithmetic and nothing about whether an SAE would learn such a structure. Tier~2 attacks that gap, but on a clean 20-feature tree with 9 edges and no injected pathologies rather than on the pathology-injected world Tier~1 grades, so it changes the world as well as the statistics and does not isolate training as the single moving part either. What it does isolate cleanly is blame: only what the SAE actually learned reaches the metrics, so a missed edge counts against a metric only if the SAE learned both endpoints. Tier~3 is named \emph{released} rather than \emph{real}: the rungs below are real SAEs too, really trained, and what sets this one apart is that it is a published checkpoint we did not train. That is a constraint and not only a label --- we do not control its dictionary, which is why the $S_\mathrm{res}$ column of Table~\ref{tab:gemma} exists for one layer only. It has no known answer at all. A fourth source, a Matryoshka SAE over a transformer trained on a PCFG corpus, runs through the same metrics but is not a rung: its grammar is known and nothing yet maps a latent to a grammar symbol, so it has no recovery score to license anything. It is reported beside gemma in Table~\ref{tab:sources} and Table~\ref{tab:layers}.}
  \label{tab:tiers}
  \begin{tabular}{llll}
    \toprule
    Tier & Runs on & Ground truth & Result \\
    \midrule
    1 Synthetic toy & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright hand-built statistics\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright by construction\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright 17/17 rows, 21/21 functions\strut} \\
    2 Trained toy & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright an SAE trained on a known tree\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright the tree is known\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright precision 1.00, recall 1.00\strut} \\
    3 Released SAE & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright \texttt{google/gemma-2-2b}\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright none --- human reading\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright 48 survivors read against autointerp labels\strut} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \\[2pt] \footnotesize Tier~3's dictionary is the released \texttt{gemma-2-2b-res-matryoshka-dc}. Lateral control (not a tier): 6/6 testable true edges run early block $\rightarrow$ late on the trained toy.
\end{table}

A pair no layer here graded carries its reason rather than being dropped, a layer that did not run a pair others ran shows a dash, and a pair that proposed nothing shows a candidate count of zero with the columns downstream of it blank: none of the three is the same statement as a clean pair. % [APP 3]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{What the cross-source comparison rests on, and how far to trust it.} Two questions, both of which are usually settled silently. \emph{First}, comparing base models of different depth needs a rule for pairing their layers, and the two defensible rules pick opposite ends of gemma: by block index PCFG's layers pair with gemma's L1 and L3, by relative depth $(L{+}1)/N$ with gemma's L6 and L12 and L18 and L24. Block index wins on the mean (8.8 points against 14.8), which is why it is what Figure~\ref{fig:cross-source-layer-response} draws---though the margin rests largely on one measure, and the reconstruction filter is inert on PCFG in any case. \emph{Second}, a small gap is only impressive if the measure could have been far apart. The last two columns ask that: \emph{range} is how far each measure moves across all 10 graded runs, and the ratio is the gap against it. The two readings do not agree---edges improving reconstruction is near the bottom on raw points and near the top on the ratio---so both are printed and neither is called correct. The honest summary is that the three measures with the smallest raw gaps are also the three pinned against a boundary ($\geq 2$ parents at 89--100\%, sibling redundancy at 3--6\%, the frequency control at 0--2\%), where agreement costs the two sources nothing. \textbf{On 2 shared layers none of this is a result.}}
  \label{tab:align}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
    \toprule
    Measure & Gap by layer index & Gap by rel.\ depth & Range over all runs & Gap / range \\
    \midrule
    edges carried by frequent tokens & 0.5 & 1.3 & 2.2 & 0.22 \\
    children with $\geq$ 2 parents & 0.6 & 16.1 & 74.3 & 0.01 \\
    sibling redundancy (mean Jaccard) & 1.0 & 3.4 & 11.8 & 0.08 \\
    fan-out concentration (Gini) & 5.8 & 5.2 & 7.9 & 0.73 \\
    edges improving reconstruction & 9.6 & 23.9 & 46.1 & 0.21 \\
    edges at chance for the base rate & 35.4 & 38.8 & 95.4 & 0.37 \\

  \caption{\textbf{One contaminating token position moved five of six metrics.} Means over the 5 layers graded both before and after the fix, block pair B0$\rightarrow$B1, before and after excluding the beginning-of-sequence position. Every quantity computed from that one co-firing matrix moved, and the one that is not --- a ratio over children that already have a parent --- did not. \textbf{The \emph{before} column is withdrawn} and is reproduced only to size the error.
